business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction, Ciudad de Panamá central registry; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with common-law-origin corporate doctrines under the Ley General de Sociedades, Law 4 of 2010)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (2012, Investment Chapter)
Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (2013, Investment Chapter)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 4 of 8 January 2010 (Ley General de Sociedades); Law 32 of 1927 (residual Commercial Code); Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (Panama AML/CFT framework), as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Law 195 of 2021; Executive Decree 363 of 2010; Law 52 of 27 December 2016 (bearer-share immobilization and nomination rules); Law 129 of 1 October 2020 (Beneficial Ownership Register), regulated by Executive Decree 173 of 8 October 2020 and administered through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax portal. Under Law 129/2020, a final beneficiary is any natural person holding, directly or indirectly, 10% or more of the shares, voting rights, or control of the legal entity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation (testimonio / escritura constitutiva)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member states; Consular Legalization at a Panamanian Consulate for non-Hague countries of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Resident Agent appointment letter and statutory AML/KYC acknowledgement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized before a Panamanian Notary; apostilled or consularly legalized when transmitted to foreign tax or regulatory authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO and director identification bundle (passport, national ID, proof of address, bank and professional references)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority of the UBO's or director's country of origin (civil registry, passport authority, notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague COD emerging-market origin jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Power of Attorney and chain-of-ownership share certificates for any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of origin jurisdiction and registered shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; additionally certified for use before the Registro Público de Panamá

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence: all UBOs, directors, officers, and settlement agents must be screened against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, EU/UK consolidated sanctions, Panama UAF domestic watchlists, Interpol notices, and judicial restrictive lists. PEP status of each shareholder — including office and family-lineage scope — must be evidenced before incorporation and refreshed every six months or upon any triggering event. The cash-on-delivery settlement model and local logistics remittance rails require continuous transaction-pattern review, FATF Recommendation 16 wire-transfer record-keeping, and immediate suspicious-transaction reporting (ROS) to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law 23/2015.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_statutory_threshold_note: The 10% statutory threshold applies to direct or indirect ownership or control; where no natural-person owner reaches 10%, senior management is reported as the final beneficiary.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público en Línea – Reserva de Nombre / Certificados (Registro Público de Panamá, www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official registry language is Spanish. Corporate names must be expressed in the Latin alphabet; non-Spanish coined names are accepted if transliterated and if the statutory suffix ('Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.') remains in Spanish. Distinctiveness is judged against identical and confusingly similar ('similaridad notoria') pre-existing names. Numerals, abbreviations, and invented words are permitted; names contrary to public order, morality, or state-patronage rules are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Banca / Financiera / Leasing / Crédito (prior Superintendencia de Bancos license required)
Seguros / Reaseguros / Aseguradora (prior Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros approval required)
Fondo de Inversión / Valores / Bolsa / Custodia (prior Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores approval required)
Gobierno / Presidencia / Ministerio / Nacional / Panamá (state-patronage implication barred)
Defensa / Militar / Policía / Armada / Explosivos / Nuclear (public-order bar)
Cooperativa / Asociación / Fundación (non-stock legal forms; not permitted within an S.A. name unless statutory conversion is separately registered)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant — through the resident agent or counsel — files a written Recurso de Reconsideración with the Registro Público within five business days, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, a transliteration chart, and the requested normalized suffix. If denied, a Recurso de Apelación is lodged with the Dirección General of the Registro Público within five business days. Exhaustion of administrative remedies is followed by a Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within two months of the definitive administrative act. As a parallel remedy, a fresh name-reservation certificate may be re-issued after any relevant cooling-off period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for ISIC 4791 e-commerce COD operations: the statutory registered office is the licensed resident agent's physical address in Panama; no separate local operational premises or physical stock is required because the activity is mail-order and electronic retail settlement conducted abroad. A virtual office is therefore accepted as the corporate seat, provided the resident agent retains full AML/CDD records, UBO documentation, and legal-process acceptance capacity at its licensed office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at approximately 30% to 40% within a 36-month operating cycle. The medium-risk enhanced AML tier, cash-on-delivery flows, and cross-border logistics remittance rails increase the likelihood of unannounced UAF, DGI, and registry inspections. All corporate books, share-transfer registers, UBO certificates, and AML/KYC files must be physically retrievable at the registered office within five business days.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Law on Corporations), as amended by Ley 12 de 2016 and Ley 60 de 2019; Articles 1-10 (formation), Articles 19-29 (articles of incorporation), Articles 48-50 (board of directors), and Article 58 (registered office and resident agent). Complementary application of the Código de Comercio, Articles 3-40 for commercial activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas y Bienes Muebles (Mercantile Section); online portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws), filed as an executed 'testimonio' (first notarized copy) for inscription in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The S.A. may incorporate with nominal capital of US$1,000 or higher (commonly US$10,000 divided into 100-500 registered shares); capital must be expressed in USD and may be partially paid in installments per Article 35 of Law 32/1927. No escrow account or capital deposit requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF ISIC_4791_05_COD_EMERGING_MARKET, S.A., adopted on [date] under Law 32 of 1927, as amended. 1. Share Subscription: The authorized capital of US$10,000, represented by 100 registered ordinary shares of US$100 each, is confirmed as fully subscribed by the founding shareholders and is hereby accepted. 2. Registered Office: The Company's registered office is fixed at the office of the Resident Agent, [address], Panama City, Panama, for statutory service of process. 3. Officers: The following are appointed: [Name], President/CEO; [Name], Secretary and Compliance Officer; [Name], Treasurer. They are authorized, jointly, to open bank accounts (including COD settlement accounts), execute logistics contracts, and file all constitutional instruments. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Portal Virtual (registration department online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Public Registry's virtual portal and request a 'Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre' for three alternative corporate names in Spanish. Pay the statutory search fee via electronic bank transfer to the Tesoro Nacional. The certificate must be obtained before notarization and remains valid for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the requesting incorporator
Payment receipt for search fee (approx. USD 15 per name certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected for similarity to an existing registration, the notary proposes the second or third alternative name from the same search; a new complementary search certificate may be requested with expedited processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Pacto Social
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (authorized Panamanian notary public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish in compliance with Law 32/1927. The founding shareholders or their attorney-in-fact execute the document before the notary, who then issues the 'testimonio' (first certified copy) for registry inscription. The notary verifies the resident agent agreement and the lawful purpose clause covering mail-order retail with COD settlement.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founding shareholders
Resident agent acceptance letter naming the Panamanian law firm/agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects, the instrument is amended by a supplementary deed (aclaración) before presentation; if a shareholder fails to execute, a power of attorney must be notarized and apostilled in the shareholder's country.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Pacto Social in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Personas Jurídicas y Bienes Muebles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original 'testimonio' of the notarized Pacto Social via the Public Registry's virtual portal or physical window of the Mercantile Section. Pay the official registration fee (approx. USD 350 for standard capital of US$10,000). Upon approval, the Registry issues the 'asiento' or inscription certificate, which constitutes the legal entity's proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a 'nota de prevención' (preventive note) is issued, the Company's counsel must cure the observation within 30 calendar days; if inscription is refused, an appeal may be filed with the Director General of the Public Registry within 5 business days, or the document can be corrected and re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (RUC) and franchise tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — Registro Único de Contribuyentes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, register the S.A. in the RUC within 10 business days using DGI's e-services portal (Formulario 411/14). Secure the taxpayer identification number and territorial tax classification. Within 30 days of start of operations, pay the annual franchise tax of USD 300 (importe de franquicia) through authorized banks, prorated for the first year.
required_dossiers: Certificate of inscription from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Pacto Social
Passport of legal representative and copy of resident agent agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects the RUC application for incomplete documentation, present the corrected set within the same portal session; if the territorial classification is queried, file an addendum confirming the Corporation's taxable income derives solely from Panamanian-sourced COD e-commerce operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and operational setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas (with supplementary filing at the Cámara de Comercio for certification, optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' for the registered office and any pack-and-ship warehouse facility, classifying the activity as ISIC 4791 (mail-order retail with COD). Submit the RUC certificate, lease title, and municipal form, and pay the municipal operating fee. This permit validates the physical premises for office, storage, and logistics dispatch under local commercial regulations.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed for the Panama City premises
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
Identification and RUC of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality requires reclassification of the business activity, submit an amended municipal form referencing the exact ISIC 4791 code and a summary of the COD logistics model; if the physical address is rejected, provide the lease's notarized copy and updated electrical inspection certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 4791 mail-order retail; general merchant oversight: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Empresas; municipal operational oversight: Municipio de Panamá — Dirección General de Rentas.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Licencia Comercial Municipal (Municipal Notice of Operation) for a non-industrial e-commerce and cash-on-delivery logistics coordination activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental, Sistema de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental (SEIA), established under Ley 41 de 1998 and Executive Decree 123 of 2009.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — ISIC 4791 mail-order retail with COD does not require a full EIA study (Category I or II) because it involves no industrial production, effluent discharge, or hazardous waste generation. A Category III 'Ficha de Registro Ambiental' is recommended only if the logistics warehouse exceeds 3,000 m² or the COD fleet surpasses 20 vehicles, in which case MiAMBIENTE filing is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No statutory industrial wastewater, VOC, or air emission thresholds apply to non-manufacturing retail operations. General compliance with DGNTI-COPANIT water quality standards and Executive Decree 85/2008: any sanitary wastewater from office/warehouse restrooms must connect to municipal sewerage or an approved treatment unit. Solid waste segregation and disposal of cardboard/plastic packaging under Ley 51 de 2018 and Executive Decree 539 de 2018; COD parcel packaging must avoid regulated hazardous materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Bomberos de Panamá (National Fire Department): mandatory 'Certificado de Requisitos Técnicos de Seguridad' prior to occupancy of any office or warehouse, covering automatic fire extinguishers, emergency exits, electrical load certification, and preventive maintenance logs. Municipality of Panama — Department of Building Public Registry: structural load inspection certificate for any warehouse racking systems. MITRADEL (Ministry of Labor and Workforce Development): occupational health and safety clearance under Resolution MITRADEL No. 041-2018, including work accident prevention plans and ergonomic protocols for dispatch workers, enforceable when the entity employs 10 or more workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – official portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Panamanian corporations must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) through DGI's e-Tax system after inscription in the Registro Público. The procedure requires appointing a resident legal representative, submitting the public deed and identity documents, and obtaining a digital signature certificate (Firma Digital) for electronic filings. Non-resident shareholders may act through a resident agent; no minimum paid-in capital is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists. A Sociedad Anónima is automatically taxed as a territorial corporation. Optional elective regimes include the Multinational Companies Headquarters (SEM) tax regime and the Panama International Services City regime, both administered by the Ministry of Commerce and Industries, which grant preferential tax treatment on qualifying foreign-source activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – value added type tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB (Balboa) 0 – no general turnover threshold; any person or entity engaged in taxable activities in Panama must register for ITBMS. Small taxpayers may use a simplified ITBMS regime on annual turnover not exceeding PAB 36,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under DGI Resolution No. 201-2712 and No. 202-3374 through the Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá. Invoices must be transmitted via approved REST API or web services, signed with a valid digital certificate, validated by DGI in near real-time, and printed or issued with a mandatory QR code stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS applies to (i) physical goods that are duly exported from Panama to a foreign destination and (ii) services rendered to non-resident clients for use entirely outside Panama, provided the service is not economically consumed within Panama. For cash-on-delivery e-commerce, the exporter must demonstrate that the goods were delivered abroad, that title and risk passed to the foreign buyer, and that the consideration was received from foreign sources.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera – DUA)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill issued by the international carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate from a Panamanian bank or equivalent SWIFT/FX confirmation evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Last-mile delivery confirmation or customs clearance proof from the foreign destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may disallow the zero-rating and assess the unpaid ITBMS at 7% plus monthly surcharges and fines up to 200% of the omitted tax in cases of fraud. Criminal tax evasion penalties include fines from PAB 5,000 to PAB 50,000 and imprisonment of two to five years. Customs penalties for false export declarations may also reach 20% of the FOB value of the goods, and the exporter may be retroactively stripped of all zero-rated credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts as fiscal agent under Law 102 of 1941; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the exclusive banking and currency-stability regulator; the Capitulo V of Law 42 of 2001 empowers SBP to administer official reserves and clearing. There is no Latin American-style issuing central bank: Panama is fully dollarized, the Balboa (PAB) exists only as coinage equivalent to the USD, and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) exercises limited monetary-policy functions. SBP Acuerdo 4-2015, Acuerdo 1-2015 and the Unified Rules on AML/KYC remain the definitive operational mandates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de facto and de jure convertibility for both current and capital transactions. Inbound investment, dividend repatriation, loan repayment, and internal treasury transfers denominated in USD suffer no exchange-control preapproval, no stamp duty, and no mandatory central-bank registration under the post-2016 foreign investment liberalization regime. Capital-account operations require only standard bank-level source-of-funds documentation and, where the operation exceeds the SBP reporting threshold, a periodic 'Reporte de Transacciones en Efectivo y Transferencias' (electronic FIU filing). The only structural constraint is that local legal tender is USD; the PAB is not an independent currency, so treasury accounting must reflect USD as the functional currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or repatriation requirement exists. A Panamanian Sociedad Anónima may retain 100% of export and COD receivables in USD in any SBP-licensed bank, and may use such proceeds directly to settle trade payables without any mandatory conversion ratio or customs-linked surrender window. Logistics companies and payment aggregators settling COD remittances into the S.A. must comply with the 'know your counterparty' and beneficial ownership disclosure duties imposed by SBP Acuerdo 7-2022, and with the UAF reporting rule for aggregated transfers exceeding USD 10,000 per calendar day, but no percentage of export proceeds is forced into any specified instrument.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul: Panama is an SBP-regulated, fully dollarized economy; FATF placed Panama on increased monitoring in June 2023, so all cross-border treasury flows are currently subject to enhanced correspondent-bank and SBP supervisory scrutiny.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low as primary treasury rail; Medium-High as secondary disbursement rail. Airwallex, Payoneer, Wise, and similar offshore EMI/PSP entities are not SBP-licensed banks and are therefore prohibited from operating a Panamanian deposit-taking or clearing account. They may lawfully hold funds offshore in the company's name, execute settlement to local last-mile couriers, and issue MT103-equivalent transfers, but they cannot receive cash-on-delivery remittances generated inside Panama, nor can they act as the custodian of statutory share capital. Practical blueprint: keep the S.A. local current account at an SBP bank as the collection and reconciliation hub, while using Airwallex's global payout rails to reach logistics partners in emerging markets. A local money-service business license under Decree 12 of 2017 is mandatory if the S.A. itself were to warehouse unrelated-party remittances, which is outside the described model.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Generally Mandatory In-Person or Notarially Certified Attendance. SBP Rule 4-2015 requires that for corporate customers with non-resident shareholders or enhanced-risk status, the appointed officers and ultimate beneficial owners be identified via at least one of (a) physical interview with a bank officer, (b) apostilled notarized power of attorney authorizing a resident director, or (c) videoconference architecture with transaction-aware e-signatures if the bank's compliance committee approves in writing. Completion practices show that the first account at an SBP 'high-tier' institution takes 10-15 business days and requires the original documents, a certified copy of the company registry 'ficha', the RUC certificate, and formal evidence of the beneficial owner's identity. A remote-only opening without local infrastructure is unlikely to pass large-bank due diligence in 2024-2025.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cash-on-delivery inflows for electronic retail, causing banks to suspect circular cash generation or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the underwriter with a 'Treasury Evidence Pack' containing: (i) 12-month payment-rail transaction ledger from the e-commerce platform (Shopify/WooCommerce equivalent) showing merchant order IDs; (ii) courier-level delivery confirmation slips or digital proof-of-delivery API export; (iii) monthly logistics settlement statements from the last-mile operator proving collection dates and remittances; (iv) a sworn statement issued by a Panamanian licensed public accountant ('Idóneo') reconciling the COD receivables to accounting revenue; and (v) the S.A.'s documented purchasing-invoice trail from the underlying emerging-market suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with bearer-share heritage or nominee structures common to Panama S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-grade 'Transparency Dossier': current Registro Público 'ficha' showing the exact share ledger, an updated Declaración de Beneficiario Final as filed with the UAF under Law 129 of 2020 and SBP Acuerdo 7-2022, apostilled passport copy of each UBO, sworn source-of-wealth statement, bank reference from the UBO's home banking institution, and a legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian attorney confirming no bearer shares subsist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Electronic retail with 'Cash0nDelivery' creates velocity-of-funds mismatches with initial registered capital (typically USD 10,000 or less in the foundational deposit).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 'Capital Adequacy and Working Capital Reconciliation' exhibit: shareholder loan agreements or contributed-capital minutes in notarized form; company bank statements showing seed capital; board resolution approving working-capital injection channels; escrow arrangement if applicable; and audited annual financial statements (or reviewed statements if SME) proving trade margins substantiate expected transaction volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent banks flag the S.A. because ISIC 4791 e-commerce merchants compressed into 'mail-order' have high chargeback / fraud / sanctions-screening hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An 'Operational Compliance Dossier': list of all trade counterparties and logistics providers with documented beneficial ownership, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS compliance certificates of the IT stack, geolocation and IP-fraud-screening policy, a written AML/ATF manual adopted by board resolution, and a sanctions-screening procedure aligned to OFAC, UN, and EU lists. When presented in Spanish legal form, this usually satisfies SBP-level enhanced due diligence.

banking_onboarding_sequence_steps: Constitution of board resolution appointing resident legal representative and compliance liaison.
Certification of the sucursal/company registry by Registro Público de Panamá within 90 days of issuance.
Obtain RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and any required municipality operating permit.
File pending reporting: Declaración de Beneficiario Final (UAF Form 770) and SBP Acuerdo 7-2022 registrations.
Present documents (original, apostilled) to selected SBP bank, attend interview, and execute account opening and e-banking mandates.
Complete internal compliance onboarding including sanctions screening and transaction-profiling questionnaires.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant Protocol: (1) The foreign shareholder or parent performs a direct wire instruction via SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary bank in Panama, identifying the beneficiary S.A., the exact 12-digit account number, and the RUC. (2) In Field 70 (Remittance Information), use the character-limited text 'APORTE DE CAPITAL – CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – [Entity Legal Name] – RUC [number]'; Panamanian law does not assign an official purpose-code taxonomy, but stating the operation as capital contribution avoids misclassification as financing or royalty. (3) The S.A. must retain the incoming MT103, the bank credit proof, and the board resolution approving the capital increase; all documents must be timestamped and internally archived because SBP supervisors may request them during annual compliance review. (4) No Ministry of Economy prior approval, no foreign-investment registration, and no exchange-control permit; however, the bank may require an updated shareholders' registry, the source-of-wealth letter, and the completion of the 'Declaración de Origen de Fondos' within 30 days. Funds are then available intraday and may be swept into the operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended multi-rail structure for the COD e-commerce treasury: (i) Supplier payments in USD up to USD 50,000 per transaction: SWIFT MT103 directly from the SBP bank, with Invoice Number and Purchase Order ID in Field 70; (ii) Larger or trust-critical purchases from emerging-market fabric or equipment suppliers: irrevocable Commercial + Documentary Letter of Credit (LC) issued by the Panamanian bank in favor of the beneficiary via an advising bank, with Incoterms clearly set (usually FOB or DAP), payable at sight; this avoids pre-shipment counterparty risk. (iii) Logistic-payout remittances in small ticket volumes: use the Airwallex or equivalent global account formatted as an on-behalf-of file, sweeping from the domestic operational account into the EMI, which then executes local-currency payouts to couriers in Colombia, Peru, Mexico, or China; the MT103 or SEPA/SEPA-INST equivalent must include the PANAMANIAN entity name consistent with the underlying logistics agreement. (iv) Local clearing of Panamanian collections operates through the country's US-dollar ACH network and the low-value electronic clearing operated by the banks; define a dedicated 'collection sub-account' to keep internal account segregation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EUR forward contracts documented under ISDA 2002 with an SBP-licensed bank or its international subsidiary; permitted because Panama has no exchange control.
Deliverable USD/CNH and USD/CNY forwards for procurement from China-based suppliers, limited to commercial settlement horizon.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American currencies (COP, BRL, MXN, CLP) with offshore bank counterparties to hedge the local disbursement legs of the logistics payments, fully documented under an ISDA Master Agreement.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR or between USD and CNH for balance-sheet hedging of long-term supplier financing; the SBP bank accepts such instruments if a board-approved derivatives policy is in place.

FX options - European-style collars on USD/CNH and USD/EUR to cap procurement cost increases while retaining downside benefit; permitted under Panamanian general commercial law Law 61 of 2015 (Financial Transactions law), provided the counterparty is a regulated financial institution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.clearing_and_liquidity_controls_summary: The treasury architecture must separate: (A) Panamanian domestic collection accounts (Banco General, Banistmo, Banco Nacional), (B) offline settlement sweep into Airwallex for emerging-market logistics payouts, and (C) segregated capital injection and escrow tracking for the minimum capital regime. All balances should be positioned 70% in the local USD demand deposit and 30% in short-dated USD treasury-style instruments to improve bank relationship comfort under SBP's enhancing margin for FATF monitoring.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax – Tasa Única Anual
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment may be channeled through authorized local banks or the DGI e-payment portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 31 of each calendar year for companies existing on the preceding December 31; newly incorporated companies pay a prorated portion corresponding to the quarter of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts a 50% surcharge (total USD 450) if settled between February 1 and April 30, and a 100% surcharge (total USD 600) if settled on or after May 1. Failure to pay for three consecutive years empowers the Public Registry to initiate administrative strike-off and dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Return – Régimen de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Directorate of Final Beneficiaries (online filing through the Public Registry portal).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation window from January 1 to March 31; any change in shareholders or beneficial ownership occurring during the year must be updated in the statutory share register and reflected in the annual declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines of up to USD 250 per unfiled or late annual return, denial of certificates of good standing and registry 'Paz y Salvo' certificates, and administrative strike-off for prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return – Declaración de Renta Anual
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; filed electronically via the DGI e-tax system.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year corporations, due March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges and monthly interest of approximately 1% on unpaid tax; statutory fines under the Fiscal Code of up to USD 10,000; the DGI may block the issuance of tax clearance certificates for companies in arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent (private contractual filing; no direct government filing unless the corporate file address is amended at the Public Registry).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal on the incorporation anniversary or on the date stipulated in the resident-agency agreement; continuity of the agent must be maintained at all times.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lapse of a resident agent, if not replaced, permits the Public Registry to declare the company dissolved under the General Law on Corporations; the corporate file is suspended and acts cannot be registered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register Audit and Share Register Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed with a government body; kept at the registered office or with the resident agent and subject to inspection by the Public Registry and DGI.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconciliation by December 31 (or fiscal year-end) and updating within 30 days of any transfer of shares, change of directors, or appointment of officers and attorneys.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or incomplete statutory registers constitute a violation of the General Law on Corporations and may be penalized with fines and refusal to register corporate documents; directors and officer may become personally liable for non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-regulated Panamanian S.A. However, under Tax Code Article 113 (as amended by Law 17 of 2018), taxpayers with gross income exceeding USD 3 million in the preceding fiscal year must present audited financial statements with their income tax return. Banks, insurers, trust licensees and securities licensees are always subject to mandatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) for public-interest entities and large taxpayers; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para Pymes) is permitted for non-public-interest entities. Local GAAP is not a separate alternative. The Commercial Code prescribes a ten-year preservation of commercial books, while tax records carry a five-year retention period; a conservative seven-year retention policy is recommended.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 70 of 2019 and its implementing decree require every S.A. to file, during the first quarter of each year (January 1 – March 31), a final-beneficiary declaration identifying direct shareholders, percentage holdings, and any ultimate beneficial owner with 10% or more participation or effective control. Share transfers must be entered in the Register of Members and disclosed in the pending annual confirmation; changes in UBO information during the year should be updated within 30 days of occurrence.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) on Panama-source net income of Sociedades Anónimas
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or sectoral preferential rate for ISIC 4791 mail-order retail. The only effective relief is strict territoriality: foreign-source income is outside the Panamanian taxable base, and deductible expenses plus a 5-year NOL carry-forward reduce the effective burden on qualifying Panama-source operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 111 - Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically via the DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (final ISR return); advance ISR payments may be required periodically during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due by 31 March of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, it is due on the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), fiscal period, and domicile of the S.A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Panamanian RUC and the address of the licensed resident agent; foreign ultimate beneficial owners are reported by name and passport/foreign tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary ISIC/CIIU code corresponding to mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 4791; do not mislabel the activity as a passive holding because DGI will verify actual COD delivery flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source sales, including cash-on-delivery remittances, Airwallex settlements, and local logistics remittance proceeds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no permanent establishment exists in Panama during the period, report only sales sourced to Panama; foreign-source receipts are excluded under territoriality but must be shown in supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 04 - Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory cost, freight, delivery/logistics charges, payment-processing fees, commissions, and other deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses connected with the generation of Panama-source revenue; cross-border related-party fees must satisfy transfer-pricing documentation requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after cost of sales, deductions, NOL carry-forwards, and any territorial-source adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned S.A. whose sales are entirely foreign-source should report zero or nil taxable income and attach a concise territorial-source explanation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 06 - ISR Payable and Withholding Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed ISR at 25%, less advance payments, employee income-tax withholdings, and other creditable withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle any balance in USD/PAB through the DGI e-Tax portal; foreign tax credits are generally not available due to the territorial system.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts surcharges of 5% to 10% of the assessed tax, monthly default interest of 1%, and possible suspension of the RUC and operations license. False or fraudulent returns attract criminal tax-evasion sanctions, fines, and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% on dividends paid out of Panama-source profits already subject to 25% ISR; 10% on dividends paid out of untaxed, exempt, or foreign-source profits. No additional tax is imposed on the non-resident shareholder receipt if the correct withholding has been made.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited DTA network. To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the payor a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a beneficial-ownership declaration, and a completed treaty-relief application, and the payor files it with the DGI before honoring the reduced rate. If no DGI approval is obtained, statutory 5% or 10% withholding must be applied and excess tax reclaimed by refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP and technical assistance: statutory 12.5% withholding on gross Panamanian-source royalties, with treaty rates usually 0%-10% where a DTA applies. Interest paid to non-residents on Panama-source debt obligations: statutory 5% generally, with treaty rates typically 5%-10%; interest on foreign-bank facilities may be exempt or reduced under domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File, Master File, and annual transfer-pricing return (Form 205) for taxpayers with gross revenue of PAB/USD 3,000,000 or more in the preceding year, or with controlled transactions exceeding PAB/USD 1,000,000 in the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to entities carrying on relevant activities, including distribution/service centres, logistics management, IP holding, and pure equity participation. A mail-order COD e-commerce S.A. must demonstrate real staff, physical premises, local board decisions, and core income-generating activities in Panama; otherwise the DGI may treat it as a shell, deny a tax-residence certificate, and impose substance-related penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting COD cash receipts from the accounting records, depositing Airwallex or local logistics remittances into personal accounts, issuing false invoices, or destroying delivery logs to underreport Panama-source e-commerce sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Panamanian fiscal law is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax, plus monthly late-payment interest of 1% and cancellation of the RUC/operations license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for fraudulent returns and unpaid withholding taxes; courts may pierce the corporate veil, imposing civil restitution, travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment where the S.A. is a mere alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Panamanian S.A. with no physical office, employees, local management, or board minutes; using the resident agent only as a letterbox while actual COD operations and decisions occur abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's ESR and entity-registry rules impose administrative fines ranging from USD 10,000 to USD 100,000 for first and repeat breaches, together with possible registration cancellation, loss of tax-residence status, and denial of treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who certify false substance declarations face personal fines, director disqualification, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced for sham incorporation and the shareholders may be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring COD receipts and Airwallex/local-logistics remittances to evade suspicious-transaction thresholds, commingling customer funds with shareholder funds, or failing to conduct basic KYC on collection agents and logistics partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's AML framework (Law 23 of 2015 and Penal Code provisions) penalises money laundering with fines up to USD 500,000 and imprisonment of 5 to 10 years; the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) may impose administrative penalties and freeze bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners are subject to criminal indictment, personal asset forfeiture, civil restitution, travel bans, and prison terms; the corporate veil does not shield knowing participants in payment-rail abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or economic distributions to foreign shareholders without applying the statutory 5%/10% Panamanian dividend withholding tax, or disguising dividends as related-party management fees to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agents are liable for the unwithheld amount, a non-compliance penalty of up to 10% of the omitted tax, and monthly default interest; the DGI may recharacterise artificial fees as dividends and deny the related deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise distributions without withholding are personally liable to restore the unlawful distributions, face civil and criminal claims, travel bans, and director disqualification, and can be joined personally in DGI enforcement actions.
